'''Lawrence Edward Roberts III''' (born October 20, 1982) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=9}}, he played at the [[power forward]] position.

==College career==
Roberts attended [[Baylor University]] for two seasons, where he made the Big 12 All-Freshman Team,<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=10410&ATCLID=1516529 | title=Men's Basketball Coaches' All-Big 12 Team Announced for 2001–02 | publisher=big12sports.com | date=March 6, 2002}}</ref> but transferred to [[Mississippi State University]] in 2003 following the [[Baylor University basketball scandal|basketball scandal]] that rocked Baylor's program that year. He was a first-team All-American and the [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]] in 2004, leading Mississippi State to its first top-two seeding in the NCAA tournament. In the 2003–04 season he averaged 16.9 points and 10.1 rebounds. He was first-team All-SEC and a first-team All-American,<ref>{{cite news |date=March 24, 2004 |title=Roberts, Childress, Gomes round out top five |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=1766339 |access-date=February 8, 2024 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref> finishing third to [[Jameer Nelson]] and [[Emeka Okafor]] for national player of the year honors. In the 2004–05 season he averaged 16.9 points and 11 rebounds. He recorded the first [[triple-double]] in Mississippi State history against [[Nicholls State University]] with 18 points, 11 rebounds, and 12 assists, while wearing an irritating translucent plastic face mask to protect his broken nose.<ref>{{cite news |date=November 21, 2004 |title=All-American finishes with 18 pts., 12 assists, 11 boards |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=243260344 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190106211423/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=243260344 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 6, 2019 |access-date=February 8, 2024 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===NBA===
Roberts was a second round draft pick (55th overall) of the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] in the [[2005 NBA draft]], but was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for two future second-round draft picks and cash considerations. He signed a contract on July 10, 2005.

===Europe===
After two seasons with the Grizzlies, in July 2007, Roberts moved to [[Europe]] and signed with Greek powerhouse [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/14417/180/item | title=Reds add Vasiliadis, Roberts, Mavrokefalidis | publisher=euroleague.net | date=July 12, 2007}}</ref> However, in October 2007, he was released from his contract before the season started.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/15760/180/item | title=Olympiacos: Roberts released, Vassiliadis hurt | publisher=euroleague.net | date=October 4, 2007}}</ref>

Without a club and not playing competitive basketball for several months, Roberts was signed by Serbian team [[KK Crvena zvezda]] on September 17, 2008, for a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/news/ | title=Red Star inks forward Lawrence Roberts | publisher=eurocupbasketball.com | date=September 17, 2008}}</ref>

On September 25, 2009, Roberts signed the [[Indiana Pacers]] training camp roster, but he got released less than a month later on October 19, 2009.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.indystar.com/article/20091019/SPORTS04/91019025/Pacers-release-3-players-in-roster-trim | title=Pacers release 3 players in roster trim | publisher=indystar.com | date=October 19, 2009}}</ref>

Two days later, on October 21, 2009, Roberts signed a one-year contract with [[KK Partizan]].<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/59437/180/item | title=Partizan signs big man Lawrence Roberts | publisher=euroleague.net | date=October 21, 2009}}</ref> With Partizan he won the 2009–10 Serbian National Championship, the 2010 Serbian National Cup, the 2010 Adriatic League and took 4th place at the [[Euroleague Basketball|Euroleague]]'s Final Four in Paris.

In July 2010, Roberts signed with the Turkish team [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Efes Pilsen]].<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/74234/efes-pilsen-lands-rebounder-roberts | title=Efes Pilsen lands rebounder Roberts | publisher=euroleague.net | date=July 28, 2010}}</ref>

On July 12, 2011, Roberts signed with [[BC Lietuvos rytas]].<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/86655/180/item | title=Lietuvos Rytas lands Roberts | publisher=euroleague.net | date=July 12, 2011}}</ref>

In July 2012, he signed with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bayern Munich officially tabs Lawrence Roberts |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/germany/41014/bayern-munich-officially-tabs-lawrence-roberts.html |access-date=August 24, 2012 |work=Sportando |archive-date=July 17, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120717073708/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/germany/41014/bayern-munich-officially-tabs-lawrence-roberts.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Bayern Munich set to announce Lawrence Roberts |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/germany/40885/bayern-munich-set-to-announce-lawrence-roberts.html |access-date=August 24, 2012 |work=Sportando |archive-date=July 28, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120728065359/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/germany/40885/bayern-munich-set-to-announce-lawrence-roberts.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> In October 2013, he signed with [[Darüşşafaka Basketbol|Darüşşafaka]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Second League|TBL2]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Lawrence Roberts signs with Darusaffaka Dogus of TB2L |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/turkey/64396/lawrence-roberts-signs-with-darusaffaka-dogus-of-tb2l.html |access-date=October 2, 2013 |newspaper=Sportando.net |archive-date=October 5, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005230809/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/turkey/64396/lawrence-roberts-signs-with-darusaffaka-dogus-of-tb2l.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On October 2, 2014, Roberts signed with [[BCM Gravelines]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]]<ref>{{cite news|title=Gravelines sign Lawrence Roberts, ex Darussafaka|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/France/basketball.aspx?NewsID=378440|access-date=October 3, 2014|work=Eurobasket.com|date=October 2, 2014}}</ref> averaging 4.7 points and 4.9 rebounds. On February 4, 2015, Roberts left the team citing personal reasons.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/151188/lawrence-roberts-leaves-gravelines-dunkerque.html Lawrence Roberts leaves Gravelines-Dunkerque]</ref>

==Personal==
{{BLP unsourced section|date=February 2021}}
Roberts is the son of Lawrence E. "Butch" Jr., and Cynthia Roberts, nephew of former sportscaster [[Robin Roberts (newscaster)|Robin Roberts]] of ''[[Good Morning America]]'' fame and grandson of the late Col. [[Lawrence E. Roberts]] Sr. and Lucimarian Roberts.
